Functions

plot_interval <- function(data, var, trim = 0.99,
                          xlab = "days", ylab = "cases") {
  x <- dplyr::pull(data, {{ var }})
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]

  stats <- tibble(stat = c("mean", "median"),
                  value = c(mean(x), median(x)))

  ggplot(data, aes({{ var }})) +
    geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, boundary = -0.5,
                   fill = "grey80", colour = "white") +
    geom_vline(data = stats, aes(xintercept = value, colour = stat, linetype = stat),
               linewidth = 0.7) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(mean = "black", median = "grey40")) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c(mean = 1, median = 2)) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = quantile(x, c(0, trim))) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = ylab, colour = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
}

## 95% highest density interval (HDI): the narrowest interval that holds 95% of
## the draws, so every value inside is more probable than every value outside.
## From coda::HPDinterval() (coda is installed with BayesianTools). Returns
## numbers: convert dates back with as.Date().
hdi <- function(x, prob = 0.95) {
  h <- coda::HPDinterval(coda::as.mcmc(as.numeric(x)), prob = prob)
  c(lo = h[1, "lower"], hi = h[1, "upper"])
}

## the HDI on the log scale, for positive quantities (parameters, rates and
## ratios). The HDI depends on the scale: on the natural scale, values close to 0
## take up almost no width, so the HDI of a quantity with a long tail towards 0
## jumps between windows and looks like spikes on a log axis.
hdi_log <- function(x, prob = 0.95) exp(hdi(log(x), prob))


theme_thesis <- theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text       = element_text(size = 11),
        legend.position  = "top")

Result 3: Hospital-community model
text:
Model


state_names <- c(
  "S_C", "E_C", "I_C_pre", "I_C_post", "R_C",
  "S_H", "E_H", "I_H_pre", "I_H_post", "Q", "R_H",
  "cum_onset_C", "cum_onset_H", "cum_noso", "cum_adm_rash", "cum_inf_C"
)

measles_ode <- function(t, y, p) {
  S_C <- y[["S_C"]]
  E_C <- y[["E_C"]]
  R_C <- y[["R_C"]]
  I_C_pre <- y[["I_C_pre"]]
  I_C_post <- y[["I_C_post"]]
  S_H <- y[["S_H"]]
  E_H <- y[["E_H"]]
  R_H <- y[["R_H"]]
  Q <- y[["Q"]]
  I_H_pre <- y[["I_H_pre"]]
  I_H_post <- y[["I_H_post"]]
  
  beta_C   <- p[["beta_C"]]
  beta_H  <- p[["beta_H"]]
  xi_alpha <- p[["xi_alpha"]]
  alpha   <- p[["alpha"]]
  p_a      <- p[["p_a"]]
  p_i     <- p[["p_i"]]
  sigma    <- p[["sigma"]]
  eta     <- p[["eta"]]
  gamma <- p[["gamma"]]
  delta    <- p[["delta"]]
  delta_M <- p[["delta_M"]]
  
  ## ---- forces of infection
  N_C     <- S_C + E_C + I_C_pre + I_C_post + R_C
  N_H_mix <- S_H + E_H + I_H_pre + I_H_post + R_H
  
  lambda_C <- beta_C * (I_C_pre + I_C_post) / N_C
  lambda_H <- if (N_H_mix > 0) beta_H * (I_H_pre + I_H_post) / N_H_mix else 0   # no hospital: no ward infections
  
  ## ---- community
  dS_C      <- -lambda_C * S_C - xi_alpha * S_C + delta * S_H
  
  dE_C      <-  lambda_C * S_C - sigma * E_C - xi_alpha * E_C + delta * E_H
  
  ## I_C_pre leaves by four routes: rash onset splits three ways, plus general
  ## admission. The three onset coefficients sum to eta.
  dI_C_pre  <-  sigma * E_C -
    (1 - p_a) * eta * I_C_pre -          # -> I_C_post
    p_a * (1 - p_i) * eta * I_C_pre -    # -> I_H_post
    p_a * p_i * eta * I_C_pre -          # -> Q
    xi_alpha * I_C_pre +                 # -> I_H_pre
    delta * I_H_pre                      # <- I_H_pre
  
  dI_C_post <-  (1 - p_a) * eta * I_C_pre -          # <- I_C_pre
    gamma * I_C_post
  
  dR_C      <-  gamma * I_C_post - alpha * R_C + delta * R_H + delta_M * Q
  
  ## ---- hospital
  dS_H      <-  xi_alpha * S_C - lambda_H * S_H - delta * S_H
  
  dE_H      <-  lambda_H * S_H + xi_alpha * E_C - sigma * E_H - delta * E_H
  
  ## I_H_pre leaves by three routes: rash onset splits two ways, plus discharge.
  ## The two onset coefficients sum to eta.
  dI_H_pre  <-  sigma * E_H +
    xi_alpha * I_C_pre -                 # <- I_C_pre
    (1 - p_i) * eta * I_H_pre -          # -> I_H_post
    p_i * eta * I_H_pre -                # -> Q
    delta * I_H_pre                      # -> I_C_pre
  
  dI_H_post <-  (1 - p_i) * eta * I_H_pre +          # <- I_H_pre
    p_a * (1 - p_i) * eta * I_C_pre -    # <- I_C_pre
    gamma * I_H_post
  
  dQ        <-  p_i * eta * I_H_pre +                # <- I_H_pre
    p_a * p_i * eta * I_C_pre -          # <- I_C_pre
    delta_M * Q
  
  dR_H      <-  gamma * I_H_post + alpha * R_C - delta * R_H
  
  ## ---- cumulative trackers -------------------------------------------------
  dcum_onset_C  <- eta * I_C_pre          # all community rash onsets
  dcum_onset_H  <- eta * I_H_pre          # admissions, rash appeared AFTER arrival
  dcum_noso     <- lambda_H * S_H         # infections acquired as an inpatient
  dcum_adm_rash <- p_a * eta * I_C_pre    # admissions, rash present on arrival
  dcum_inf_C    <- lambda_C * S_C         # infections acquired in the community
  
  ## names are documentation: deSolve reads this by position, so the order must
  ## match state_names. The check below enforces that.
  list(
    c(
      S_C = dS_C,
      E_C = dE_C,
      I_C_pre = dI_C_pre,
      I_C_post = dI_C_post,
      R_C = dR_C,
      S_H = dS_H,
      E_H = dE_H,
      I_H_pre = dI_H_pre,
      I_H_post = dI_H_post,
      Q = dQ,
      R_H = dR_H,
      cum_onset_C = dcum_onset_C,
      cum_onset_H = dcum_onset_H,
      cum_noso = dcum_noso,
      cum_adm_rash = dcum_adm_rash,
      cum_inf_C = dcum_inf_C
    )
  )
}

Helpers.
p_i is fixed rather than estimated: it only changes how long I_H_post transmits, which the case series barely sees. It is varied in a sensitivity analysis instead.

p_i_fixed <- 0.9

## s_C0 and s_H0 are fixed inputs, set in the Parameters section. seed is the
## number of latent infections in the community at t = 0.
init_state <- function(seed) {
  y <- c(
    S_C = s_C0 * N_C0 - seed, E_C = seed,
    I_C_pre = 0, I_C_post = 0, R_C = (1 - s_C0) * N_C0,
    S_H = s_H0 * N_H0, E_H = 0, I_H_pre = 0, I_H_post = 0, Q = 0,
    R_H = (1 - s_H0) * N_H0,
    cum_onset_C = 0, cum_onset_H = 0, cum_noso = 0,
    cum_adm_rash = 0, cum_inf_C = 0
  )
  y[state_names]
}

## ODE parameters from the fitted parameters. xi_alpha and alpha depend only on
## the fixed s_C0 and s_H0, so they are computed once, in the Parameters section.
make_params <- function(par) {
  c(beta_C = par[["beta_C"]], beta_H = par[["kappa"]] * par[["beta_C"]],
    xi_alpha = xi_alpha, alpha = alpha,
    p_a = par[["p_a"]],
    p_i = if ("p_i" %in% names(par)) par[["p_i"]] else p_i_fixed,
    delta = delta, delta_M = delta_M,
    sigma = sigma, eta = eta, gamma = gamma)
}

solve_model <- function(par, times) {
  out <- tryCatch(
    ode(y = init_state(par[["seed"]]),
        times = times, func = measles_ode,
        parms = make_params(par),
        method = "lsoda", atol = 1e-3, rtol = 1e-6),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(out) || nrow(out) != length(times) || anyNA(out)) return(NULL)
  out
}

## weekly quantities. The two case types partition all rash onsets:
##   adm_w  = p_a * onset_C + onset_H   children admitted with measles
##   out_w  = (1 - p_a) * onset_C       community cases not admitted
run_model <- function(par, n_weeks, full = FALSE) {

  sol <- solve_model(par, seq.int(0L, n_weeks * 7L, by = 7L))
  if (is.null(sol)) return(NULL)

  onset_C  <- diff(sol[, "cum_onset_C"])
  onset_H  <- diff(sol[, "cum_onset_H"])
  adm_rash <- diff(sol[, "cum_adm_rash"])

  if (!full) {
    return(list(adm = adm_rash + onset_H,
                out = onset_C - adm_rash))
  }

  keep <- -1L   # drop t = 0, so each row pairs with one diff()

  tibble(
    week     = seq_len(n_weeks),
    onset_C  = onset_C,
    onset_H  = onset_H,
    adm      = adm_rash + onset_H,
    out      = onset_C - adm_rash,
    noso     = diff(sol[, "cum_noso"]),
    inf_C    = diff(sol[, "cum_inf_C"]),
    I_H_pre  = sol[keep, "I_H_pre"],
    I_H_post = sol[keep, "I_H_post"],
    Q        = sol[keep, "Q"],
    N_H      = rowSums(sol[keep, c("S_H", "E_H", "I_H_pre",
                                   "I_H_post", "Q", "R_H")])
  )
}

title: Result 3: Hospital-community model
text:
Parameters
Disease natural history (rate per day):

sigma <- 1 / 8      # exposed -> infectious
eta   <- 1 / 4      # pre-rash -> post-rash
gamma <- 1 / 4      # post-rash -> removed


Hospital population and alpha_bar
Number of children 15 years and under in HCMC:

N <- df_census |>
  filter(age <= 15) |>
  pull(n) |>
  sum()

cat("Total population N:", N)

Total population N: 1388365


Children’s Hospital 1 reported 90,000 admissions per year. Assume HCMC total is 5 times CH1, of which 40% are HCMC residents. Mean length of stay 5.2 days.
alpha_bar is admissions per community child per day, because in the ODE the admission flows multiply community compartments. Working from the admission count avoids needing N_C0 before alpha_bar is known, and makes the disease-free state balance exactly.

resident_frac <- 0.4
delta         <- 1 / 5.2

adm_per_day <- 5 * resident_frac * 90000 / 365
N_H0        <- adm_per_day / delta
N_C0        <- N - N_H0
alpha_bar   <- adm_per_day / N_C0

s_C0 <- 0.08
s_H0 <- 0.29
xi       <- (s_H0 * (1 - s_C0)) / (s_C0 * (1 - s_H0))
alpha    <- alpha_bar / (1 + s_C0 * (xi - 1))
xi_alpha <- xi * alpha



p_a and the instantaneous-admission assumption
The model admits a fraction p_a of community cases at rash onset, with no delay. That is justified only if the observed onset-to-admission interval is short. HCMC records a median of 0 days; the Hanoi line list is shown here for comparison.

d <- df_hn |>
  mutate(ad_delay = as.numeric(admission_date - onset_date)) |>
  filter(!is.na(ad_delay), ad_delay >= 0, ad_delay <= 10,
         source_province == "community", province == "Ha Noi")

d |> summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(ad_delay), median = median(ad_delay))

    n     mean median
1 399 2.142857      2

plot_interval(d, ad_delay, trim = 0.99,
              xlab = "onset to admission delay (days)", ylab = "cases")










delta_M
Discharge rate from isolation, from measles length of stay at Children’s Hospital 2.

d <- df_ch2 |>
  mutate(stay = as.numeric(discharge - admission)) |>
  filter(!is.na(stay), stay >= 0, stay < 30)

est <- d |> summarise(n = n(), los_M = mean(stay), median = median(stay))
est

     n    los_M median
1 3353 5.787056      5

plot_interval(d, stay, xlab = "length of stay (days)", ylab = "cases")







delta_M <- 1 / est$los_M
cat("delta_M:", round(delta_M, 4), " mean isolated stay:",
    round(1 / delta_M, 1), "days\n")

delta_M: 0.1728  mean isolated stay: 5.8 days




Structural check
Confirms the derivative vector comes back in the order state_names expects and that the population is conserved. It has to run after the constants above, because make_params and init_state read them.

local({
  par <- c(beta_C = 2.2, kappa = 0.5, p_a = 0.1, seed = 10)
  d   <- measles_ode(0, init_state(10), make_params(par))[[1]]
  stopifnot(identical(names(d), state_names))
  stopifnot(abs(sum(d)) < 1e-6)
  cat("model check: state order and conservation OK\n")
})

model check: state order and conservation OK

text:
Calibration

Options
The three fits to compare are:

total cases, as before: obs_model = "total", fit_rho = TRUE
no under-reporting: fit_rho = FALSE
inpatients and outpatients separately: obs_model = "split"


obs_model <- "total"   # "total": one negative binomial on all weekly cases
                       # "split": one each for inpatients and outpatients
fit_rho   <- T      # TRUE: estimate the reporting fraction rho
                       # FALSE: no under-reporting, rho fixed at 1

stopifnot(obs_model %in% c("total", "split"), is.logical(fit_rho))

## fitted parameters for these options
par_names <- c("beta_C", "kappa", "p_a", "seed",
               if (fit_rho) "rho",
               if (obs_model == "total") "phi" else c("phi_in", "phi_out"))
par_names

[1] "beta_C" "kappa"  "p_a"    "seed"   "rho"    "phi"   

## one file per option, so the fits can be compared later
fit_file <- sprintf("measles_fit_%s_rho%s_sC%s.rds", obs_model, fit_rho, s_C0)

Epidemic curve by inpatient and outpatient:

df_week_wide <- df_hcmc |>
  filter(age <= 15) |>
  mutate(
    date = as_date(ngay_nv),
    week = floor_date(date, "week", week_start = 1),
    type = if_else(inpatient, "inpatient", "outpatient")
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(week), !is.na(type)) |>
  count(week, type, name = "cases") |>
  complete(week = seq(min(week), max(week), by = "week"), type,
           fill = list(cases = 0)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = cases, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(total = inpatient + outpatient,
         prop_inpatient = inpatient / total) |>
  arrange(week)

n_lead_weeks <- 8      # simulated weeks before the first observed week

obs <- df_week_wide |>
  arrange(week) |>
  mutate(t_week = row_number() + n_lead_weeks)

n_weeks   <- max(obs$t_week)
obs_idx   <- obs$t_week
obs_total <- obs$total
obs_in    <- obs$inpatient
obs_out   <- obs$outpatient
t0_date   <- min(obs$week) - 7 * (n_lead_weeks + 1)

n_total <- as.integer(sum(obs$total))
n_in    <- as.integer(sum(obs$inpatient))

cat("weeks:", n_weeks, " total:", n_total, " inpatient:", n_in,
    " share:", round(n_in / n_total, 3), "\n")

weeks: 88  total: 7114  inpatient: 3743  share: 0.526 




Likelihood
Weekly reported cases follow a negative binomial distribution, with mean rho times the model’s weekly rash onsets. The options above decide how the model meets the data:

obs_model = "total": one negative binomial for all weekly cases, with mean rho * (adm + out) and dispersion phi.
obs_model = "split": one negative binomial for inpatients, with mean rho * adm, and one for outpatients, with mean rho * out. Each has its own dispersion, phi_in and phi_out.
fit_rho = FALSE: rho is fixed at 1, so every case is assumed reported.

Prior

## Bounds, prior density and prior sampler of every parameter that can be
## fitted. The options decide which ones are used (par_names).
priors <- list(
  beta_C = list(lower = 0.1, upper = 20,
                d = \(x) dunif(x, 0.1, 20, log = TRUE),
                r = \(n) runif(n, 0.1, 20)),
  kappa  = list(lower = 0, upper = 10,
                d = \(x) dunif(x, 0, 10, log = TRUE),
                r = \(n) runif(n, 0, 10)),
  p_a    = list(lower = 0.005, upper = 0.95,      # mean 0.29, deliberately wide
                d = \(x) dbeta(x, 2, 5, log = TRUE),
                r = \(n) rbeta(n, 2, 5)),
  seed   = list(lower = 1, upper = 50,
                d = \(x) dunif(x, 1, 50, log = TRUE),
                r = \(n) runif(n, 1, 50)),
  rho    = list(lower = 0.001, upper = 1,
                d = \(x) dbeta(x, 2, 8, log = TRUE),
                r = \(n) rbeta(n, 2, 8)),
  phi    = list(lower = 0.1, upper = 100,
                d = \(x) dunif(x, 0.1, 100, log = TRUE),
                r = \(n) runif(n, 0.1, 100))
)
priors$phi_in  <- priors$phi    # split option: the same prior for each series
priors$phi_out <- priors$phi

lower <- map_dbl(priors[par_names], \(p) p$lower)
upper <- map_dbl(priors[par_names], \(p) p$upper)

## base R only (mapply, not purrr): this also runs on the parallel workers,
## which load deSolve and nothing else
log_prior <- function(x) {
  sum(mapply(\(p, v) p$d(v), priors[par_names], as.numeric(x)))
}

## draw from the prior, not from the bounding box, so the DEzs archive starts
## where the prior has weight
prior_sampler <- function(n = 1) {
  m <- sapply(priors[par_names], \(p) p$r(n))
  if (n == 1) as.numeric(m) else m
}

prior <- createPrior(density = log_prior, sampler = prior_sampler,
                     lower = lower, upper = upper)

# Quiet weeks must appear as zero, or a gap reads as continuous transmission
weekly_counts <- function(data) {
  data |>
    count(week, name = "cases") |>
    complete(week = seq(min(week), max(week), by = "week"),
             fill = list(cases = 0L))
}

find_outbreaks <- function(data, threshold = ob_threshold,
                           min_run = ob_min_run, max_gap = ob_max_gap) {
  wc  <- weekly_counts(data)
  r   <- rle(wc$cases >= threshold)
  end <- cumsum(r$lengths)
  hit <- which(r$values & r$lengths >= min_run)

  if (length(hit) == 0) {
    return(tibble(episode = integer(), start = wc$week[0], end = wc$week[0],
                  weeks = integer(), cases = integer()))
  }

  s <- (end - r$lengths + 1L)[hit]
  e <- end[hit]

  tibble(s, e, grp = cumsum(c(1L, (s[-1] - head(e, -1) - 1L) >= max_gap))) |>
    summarise(i1 = min(s), i2 = max(e), .by = grp) |>
    transmute(
      episode = row_number(),
      start   = wc$week[i1],
      end     = wc$week[i2],
      weeks   = i2 - i1 + 1L,
      cases   = map2_int(i1, i2, \(a, b) sum(wc$cases[a:b])),
      peak_week  = map2_vec(i1, i2, \(a, b) wc$week[a:b][which.max(wc$cases[a:b])]),
      peak_cases = map2_int(i1, i2, \(a, b) max(wc$cases[a:b]))
    )
}

outbreak_sensitivity <- function(data, thresholds = c(3, 5, 10, 20, 30)) {
  map(thresholds, \(x) find_outbreaks(data, threshold = x) |>
        mutate(threshold = x, .before = 1)) |>
    list_rbind()
}

# rate = cases on day t / (population - cumulative cases up to day t-1).
# A daily hazard among those not yet recorded as cases, not a cumulative
# attack rate; name it accordingly in the caption.
add_attack_rate <- function(d, group, n_days = ma_days) {
  d |>
    arrange({{ group }}, date) |>
    mutate(
      at_risk = n_census - lag(cumsum(n), default = 0),
      rate    = n / at_risk,
      rate_ma = slide_mean(rate, before = n_days - 1, complete = TRUE),
      .by = {{ group }}
    )
}

    select(month, n, n_tot, pct, lab)

title: Result 1: Serosurveillance
text:
Serology
Children of vaccination age in 3 hospitals, sampled 01-08-2022 to 30-04-2024

hosp_lab <- c("Children's hospital 1"    = "CH1",
              "Children's hospital 2"    = "CH2",
              "City Children's Hospital" = "CCH")

df_sero_3ch <- df_sero |>
  filter(hospital %in% names(hosp_lab),
         between(date_collection, dmy("01-08-2022"), dmy("30-04-2024"))) |>
  mutate(hospital = factor(hosp_lab[as.character(hospital)], levels = hosp_lab))

df_sero_3ch_mod <- df_sero_3ch |>
  filter(exact_age >= 9 / 12) |>
  mutate(age_5y = factor(if_else(exact_age < 5, "<5", ">=5"), c("<5", ">=5")),
         age_ceiling = ceiling(exact_age)) |>
  left_join(df_census_age, join_by(age_ceiling == age)) |>
  mutate(weight = n_census / mean(n_census))


Hospital coverage

setdiff(df_sero_3ch$district, df_map_hcmc$district_blank)   # want character(0)

[1] NA

brks_age <- c(0, 9/12, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 15)
age_labs <- c("<9m", "9-11m", "1y", "2y", "3y", "4y", "5-9y", "10-15y")

df_age <- df_sero_3ch |>
  mutate(
    age_band = cut(exact_age, brks_age, age_labs,
                   right = FALSE, include.lowest = TRUE),
    period_lab = factor(format(period_collect, "%b %Y"),
                        levels = format(sort(unique(period_collect)), "%b %Y"))
  ) |>
  count(hospital, period_lab, age_band) |>
  complete(nesting(hospital, period_lab), age_band, fill = list(n = 0))

xmax <- max(df_age$n)

plot_hosp <- function(d, x_axis = FALSE, y_lab = FALSE) {
  ggplot(d, aes(x = n, y = age_band, fill = age_band == "<9m")) +
    geom_col() +
    facet_grid(hospital ~ period_lab, switch = "y") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey40", `TRUE` = "#D55E00"),
                      guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = c(0, xmax),
      # drop the top break, its label would sit on the panel edge
      breaks = \(l) { b <- breaks_pretty(3)(l); b[b <= 0.85 * l[2]] },
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))
    ) +
    labs(x = if (x_axis) "Number of samples" else NULL, y = "Age band") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          strip.placement = "outside",
          # NA keeps the space reserved, so only one row shows the title
          axis.title.y = element_text(colour = if (y_lab) "black" else NA),
          axis.text.x  = if (x_axis) element_text() else element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.x = if (x_axis) element_line() else element_blank())
}

p_list <- df_age |> group_split(hospital) |> map(droplevels)
n_h    <- length(p_list)

grobs <- p_list |>
  imap(\(d, i) plot_hosp(d, x_axis = i == n_h, y_lab = i == ceiling(n_h / 2))) |>
  map(ggplotGrob)

# Hospitals have different numbers of periods, so narrower gtables get extra
# panel and spacing columns until all of them are the same width
pan_l <- \(g) g$layout$l[startsWith(g$layout$name, "panel")]
g_ref <- grobs[[which.max(map_int(grobs, \(g) length(pan_l(g))))]]
gap   <- g_ref$widths[max(pan_l(g_ref)) - 1]

pad_to <- function(g, target) {
  need <- target - ncol(g)
  if (need <= 0) return(g)
  pos <- max(pan_l(g))
  w   <- rep(list(gap, unit(1, "null")), length.out = need)
  if (need %% 2 == 1) w[[need]] <- unit(0, "cm")
  for (i in seq_len(need)) {
    g   <- gtable_add_cols(g, w[[i]], pos)
    pos <- pos + 1
  }
  g
}

grobs       <- map(grobs, pad_to, target = max(map_int(grobs, ncol)))
grobs[-n_h] <- map(grobs[-n_h], \(g) gtable_add_rows(g, unit(4, "mm")))

p_age <- reduce(grobs, \(a, b) rbind(a, b, size = "max"))

# Map margins matched to the space above the first and below the last panel
cm_h  <- \(u) convertHeight(u, "cm", valueOnly = TRUE)
pan_t <- \(g) g$layout$t[startsWith(g$layout$name, "panel")][1]
m_top <- cm_h(sum(grobs[[1]]$heights[seq_len(pan_t(grobs[[1]]) - 1)]))
m_bot <- cm_h(sum(grobs[[n_h]]$heights[-seq_len(pan_t(grobs[[n_h]]))]))

pct_min <- 1                                             # below this % draws grey
mid     <- 100 / n_distinct(df_map_hcmc$district_blank)  # equal-share reference

df_map_pct <- df_sero_3ch |>
  count(hospital, district) |>
  complete(hospital, district = df_map_hcmc$district_blank, fill = list(n = 0)) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n), .by = hospital) |>
  mutate(lfc = if_else(pct >= pct_min, log2(pct / mid), NA)) |>
  left_join(select(df_map_hcmc, district_blank),
            join_by(district == district_blank)) |>
  st_as_sf()

lo <- log2(pct_min / mid)                # bar starts exactly at pct_min
hi <- max(df_map_pct$lfc, na.rm = TRUE)

brks_pct <- c(1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 40)
brks_pct <- brks_pct[brks_pct >= pct_min & log2(brks_pct / mid) <= hi]

p_map_col <- df_map_pct |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = lfc), colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.15) +
  facet_wrap(~ hospital, ncol = 1) +
  coord_sf(expand = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours  = pal_gsea()(12),
    limits   = c(lo, hi),
    na.value = "grey88",
    rescaler = \(x, to = c(0, 1), from = range(x, na.rm = TRUE))
                 rescale_mid(x, to, from, mid = 0),
    breaks   = log2(brks_pct / mid),
    labels   = paste0(brks_pct, "%"),
    name     = "% of samples",
    guide    = guide_colourbar(
      theme = theme(legend.key.height = unit(2.6, "cm"),
                    legend.key.width  = unit(0.35, "cm"))
    )
  ) +

slot_name <- function(d) {
  a <- min(d); b <- max(d)
  case_when(a == b             ~ format(a, "%b %Y"),
            year(a) == year(b) ~ str_c(format(a, "%b"), "-", format(b, "%b %Y")),
            .default           = str_c(format(a, "%b %Y"), "-", format(b, "%b %Y")))

         slot_id = cumsum(gap > slot_gap)) |>
  mutate(slot = slot_name(period_collect), .by = slot_id)

fit_age <- function(d) {
  nu <- n_distinct(d$exact_age)
  if (nrow(d) < 10 || nu < 4) return(NULL)      # too thin for a smooth
  gam(pos ~ s(exact_age, k = max(3, min(10, nu - 1))),
      family = binomial, data = d, method = "REML") |>
    predict_ci(d, "exact_age")
}

panel_age <- function(h, s) {
  d_pt <- filter(rug_age, hospital == h, slot == s)
  if (nrow(d_pt) == 0) return(plot_spacer())
  d_pr <- filter(pred_age, hospital == h, slot == s)

  ggplot() +
    geom_point(data = d_pt, aes(exact_age, pos), shape = 124, alpha = 0.3) +
    geom_ribbon(data = d_pr,
                aes(exact_age, ymin = lwr_true, ymax = upr_true, fill = agegr),
                alpha = 0.15, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_line(data = d_pr,
              aes(exact_age, fit_true, colour = agegr, linetype = lab_gam,
                  group = 1)) +
    facet_wrap(~strip) +
    # top break dropped, its label would collide with the next panel's zero
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, x_age[2] - 1, 5), limits = x_age,
                       expand = expansion(mult = 0.02)) +
    labs(x = if (h == end_h && s == mid_slot) "Age (years)" else NULL, y = NULL) +
    layers_sero +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
}

  g

# ---- Helpers --------------------------------------------------------
prev_correct <- function(est_val, sens, spec) {
  (est_val + spec - 1) / (sens + spec - 1)
}

clamp01 <- function(x) pmin(pmax(x, 0), 1)

# Vectorised prop.test CI (Wilson score with continuity correction)
prop_ci <- function(x, n, conf = 0.95) {
  z     <- qnorm((1 + conf) / 2)
  est   <- x / n
  yates <- pmin(0.5, abs(x - n / 2))
  z22n  <- z^2 / (2 * n)
  pc_u  <- est + yates / n
  pc_l  <- est - yates / n
  su    <- pmin(pc_u, 1)
  sl    <- pmax(pc_l, 0)
  tibble(
    ci_lwr = if_else(pc_l <= 0, 0,
                     clamp01((sl + z22n - z * sqrt(sl * (1 - sl) / n + z22n / (2 * n))) / (1 + 2 * z22n))),
    ci_upr = if_else(pc_u >= 1, 1,
                     clamp01((su + z22n + z * sqrt(su * (1 - su) / n + z22n / (2 * n))) / (1 + 2 * z22n)))
  )
}

predict_ci <- function(model, data, var, ci = 0.95, n_grid = 200) {
  link_inv <- model$family$linkinv
  df_res   <- nrow(data) - length(model$coefficients)
  tq       <- qt(1 - (1 - ci) / 2, df_res)
  rng      <- range(data[[var]], na.rm = TRUE)
  newd     <- tibble(!!var := seq(rng[1], rng[2], length.out = n_grid))
  pr       <- predict(model, newdata = newd, se.fit = TRUE, type = "link")
  newd |>
    mutate(
      fit = link_inv(pr$fit),
      lwr = link_inv(pr$fit - tq * pr$se.fit),
      upr = link_inv(pr$fit + tq * pr$se.fit)
    )
}

adjust_prev <- function(d) {
  d |>
    mutate(across(c(fit, lwr, upr),
                  \(x) clamp01(prev_correct(x, sens, spec)),
                  .names = "{.col}_true"))
}

# Nearest grid point to each reference age, from the pooled ("All periods")
# fit per hospital.
 
ref_ages <- c(1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 15)
 
pred_age |>
  filter(period_lab == lab_all) |>
  cross_join(tibble(ref = ref_ages)) |>
  slice_min(abs(exact_age - ref), n = 1, by = c(hospital, ref)) |>
  mutate(lab = sprintf("%s%% (%s to %s)",
                       pc(fit_true), pc(lwr_true), pc(upr_true))) |>
  select(hospital, ref, age = exact_age, fit_true, lab) |>
  arrange(hospital, ref) |>
  print(n = Inf)
 
# minimum of the pooled curve and where it occurs: the susceptibility trough
pred_age |>
  filter(period_lab == lab_all) |>
  slice_min(fit_true, n = 1, by = hospital) |>
  mutate(lab = sprintf("%s%% (%s to %s) at age %.1f y",
                       pc(fit_true), pc(lwr_true), pc(upr_true), exact_age)) |>
  select(hospital, exact_age, fit_true, lab) |>
  print(n = Inf)
 
# age range over which the fitted curve sits below the critical threshold
pred_age |>
  filter(period_lab == lab_all, fit_true < critp) |>
  summarise(age_from = min(exact_age), age_to = max(exact_age),
            n_grid = n(), .by = hospital) |>
  print(n = Inf)
 
# and where the upper CI is entirely below it, which is the stronger claim
pred_age |>
  filter(period_lab == lab_all, upr_true < critp) |>
  summarise(age_from = min(exact_age), age_to = max(exact_age), .by = hospital) |>
  print(n = Inf)
 
# ---- 4. Fitted time curve: start, end, and change -------------------------
 
pred_date |>
  slice(c(which.min(date_collection), which.max(date_collection)),
        .by = c(hospital, age_5y)) |>
  mutate(point = if_else(date_collection == min(date_collection), "start", "end"),
         .by = c(hospital, age_5y)) |>
  select(hospital, age_5y, point, fit_true, lwr_true, upr_true) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = point, values_from = c(fit_true, lwr_true, upr_true)) |>
  mutate(change_pp = 100 * (fit_true_end - fit_true_start)) |>
  print(n = Inf)
 
# ---- 5. Under-5 versus 5-and-over, the headline contrast ------------------
 
df_mod |>
  summarise(npos = sum(pos), ntot = n(), .by = age_5y) |>
  mutate(prop_ci(npos, ntot)) |>
  mutate(prev_true = clamp01(prev_correct(npos / ntot, sens, spec)),
         lwr_true  = clamp01(prev_correct(ci_lwr, sens, spec)),
         upr_true  = clamp01(prev_correct(ci_upr, sens, spec)),
         lab = sprintf("%s%% (%s to %s), %d/%d",
                       pc(prev_true), pc(lwr_true), pc(upr_true), npos, ntot)) |>
  select(age_5y, lab) |>
  print()
 
# ---- 6. Sentence-ready strings --------------------------------------------
 
pred_age |>
  filter(period_lab == lab_all) |>
  slice_min(fit_true, n = 1, by = hospital) |>
  mutate(txt = sprintf("%s: fitted seroprevalence reaches a minimum of %s%% (%s to %s) at age %.1f years",
                       hospital, pc(fit_true), pc(lwr_true), pc(upr_true), exact_age)) |>
  pull(txt) |>
  writeLines()

# VE point estimates and 95% CIs (Malfait et al. 1994; Uzicanin & Zimmerman
# 2011; Yeung et al. 2005). SHELF::fitdist() fits a beta to each, with the
# estimate as the 50th percentile and the CI limits as the 2.5th and 97.5th,
# by least squares on the cumulative probabilities. Two parameters for three
# values, so the fit is close but not exact (check below). VE depends on dose
# count, not a product across doses, because the MCV2 estimate is a two-dose
# effectiveness.
ve_beta <- tribble(
  ~param,  ~lo,   ~est,  ~hi,
  "ve1_L", 0.796, 0.865, 0.915,   # MCV1 given at 9-11 months
  "ve1_H", 0.841, 0.944, 0.980,   # MCV1 given at 12 months or later
  "ve2",   0.920, 0.986, 0.994    # two doses
) |>
  mutate(SHELF::fitdist(vals = c(lo, est, hi), probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975),
                        lower = 0, upper = 1)$Beta,
         .by = param)

# Each child contributes one interval, so counting is a +1/-1 event table plus
# a cumsum: O(children), not O(children x weeks). key adds a dose-week
# dimension, which is what lets
#   sum_i VE_i(w) = mult * exp(-q w) * sum_s N[w, s] exp(q s)
# be evaluated with two small matrix products per term instead of m_draws
# passes over the registry.
count_intervals <- function(a, b, g, ng, key = rep(1L, length(a))) {
  a  <- pmax(a, 1L)
  b  <- pmin(b, n_week)
  ok <- !is.na(a) & !is.na(b) & !is.na(g) & !is.na(key) & b >= a
  if (!any(ok)) return(list(n = matrix(0, n_week, ng), z = 0L, nk = 1L))
  a <- a[ok]; b <- b[ok]; g <- g[ok]; key <- key[ok]

  z   <- min(key):max(key)
  nk  <- length(z)
  nb  <- ng * nk * (n_week + 1L)
  off <- ((g - 1L) * nk + (key - z[1L])) * (n_week + 1L)
  d   <- tabulate(off + a, nb) - tabulate(off + b + 1L, nb)

  n <- matrix(d, nrow = n_week + 1L) |> apply(2, cumsum)
  list(n = n[seq_len(n_week), , drop = FALSE], z = z, nk = nk)
}

cover <- function(a, b, g, ng) count_intervals(a, b, g, ng)$n

term_matrices <- function(a, b, g, key, mult, ng) {
  kc <- count_intervals(a, b, g, ng, key)
  Ez <- exp(outer(kc$z, q_wk))                 # n_key  x M
  Ew <- exp(outer(seq_len(n_week), -q_wk))     # n_week x M
  map(seq_len(ng), \(gg) {
    cols <- ((gg - 1L) * kc$nk + 1L):(gg * kc$nk)
    (kc$n[, cols, drop = FALSE] %*% Ez) * Ew * rep(mult, each = n_week)
  })
}

build_series <- function(grp) {
  lev <- levels(droplevels(grp))
  ng  <- length(lev)
  gi  <- as.integer(factor(as.character(grp), levels = lev))

  mk <- function(entry, exit, vax, dose_lab) {
    b   <- wk_ge(exit) - 1L
    a_d <- wk_ge(entry)
    a_n <- pmax(a_d, wk_ge(vax))      # doses before entry count from entry
    tibble(
      week    = rep(weeks, times = ng),
      region  = rep(lev, each = n_week),
      dose    = dose_lab,
      n_denom = as.vector(cover(a_d, b, gi, ng)),
      n_vax   = as.vector(cover(a_n, b, gi, ng))
    )
  }

  cov_df <- bind_rows(
    mk(child$t9,  child$t60, child$d1, "Dose 1"),
    mk(child$t18, child$t60, child$d2, "Dose 2")
  ) |>
    mutate(region = factor(region, levels = lev),
           coverage = if_else(n_denom > 0, n_vax / n_denom, NA))

  numM <- replicate(ng, matrix(0, n_week, m_draws), simplify = FALSE)
  for (bb in 1:2) {                                   # single-dose periods
    sel <- which(!is.na(s_first) & band_first == bb)
    if (length(sel)) numM <- Map(`+`, numM, term_matrices(
      pmax(a_den, s_first)[sel], b_one[sel], gi[sel], s_first[sel],
      if (bb == 1L) draws$ve1_L else draws$ve1_H, ng))
  }
  sel <- which(!is.na(s_second))                      # two-dose periods
  if (length(sel)) numM <- Map(`+`, numM, term_matrices(
    pmax(a_den, s_second)[sel], b_exit[sel], gi[sel], s_second[sel],
    draws$ve2, ng))

  denE <- cover(a_den, b_exit, gi, ng)

  evc_df <- map2(seq_len(ng), lev, \(gg, nm) {
    E  <- numM[[gg]] / na_if(denE[, gg], 0L)
    qs <- apply(E, 1, quantile, probs = c(0.5, evc_band), na.rm = TRUE)
    tibble(week = weeks, region = nm,
           evc = qs[1, ], evc_lo = qs[2, ], evc_hi = qs[3, ])
  }) |>
    list_rbind() |>
    mutate(region = factor(region, levels = lev))

  idx <- which(weeks >= win_start & weeks <= win_end)

  # Point = median of the period mean across draws. Bar = lowest weekly lower
  # band to highest weekly upper band, so it covers both the change over the
  # window and the VE uncertainty.
  evc_win <- map2(seq_len(ng), lev, \(gg, nm) {
    dsum <- sum(denE[idx, gg])
    pa   <- if (dsum > 0) colSums(numM[[gg]][idx, , drop = FALSE]) / dsum
            else rep(NA_real_, m_draws)
    w    <- evc_df$region == nm & between(evc_df$week, win_start, win_end)
    tibble(region = nm,
           x    = median(pa),
           x_lo = min(evc_df$evc_lo[w], na.rm = TRUE),
           x_hi = max(evc_df$evc_hi[w], na.rm = TRUE))
  }) |>
    list_rbind()

  cov_win <- cov_df |>
    filter(between(week, win_start, win_end), n_denom > 0) |>
    summarise(x = sum(n_vax) / sum(n_denom),
              x_lo = min(coverage), x_hi = max(coverage),
              .by = c(region, dose))

  list(cov = cov_df, evc = evc_df, cov_win = cov_win, evc_win = evc_win)
}

make_x_breaks <- function(rng, by = "3 months", min_gap_days = 70) {

           as.numeric(rng[2] - inner)  >= min_gap_days
  sort(unique(c(rng[1], inner[keep], rng[2])))

  scale_x_date(breaks = x_breaks, labels = label_month_year,
               expand = expansion(mult = 0.03)) +

# Horizontal bar = range of weekly values over the window. For EVC it runs
# from the lowest weekly lower band to the highest weekly upper band, so it
# includes the VE uncertainty. Vertical bar = 95% CI for seroprevalence.
# Dotted diagonal = 1:1. It only enters a panel where the x and y ranges
# overlap, which they do not here, so the y limit is extended just enough for
# the line to cross the top-left corner.
diag_lim <- scat |>
  summarise(x  = min(x_lo, na.rm = TRUE),
            x2 = max(x_hi, na.rm = TRUE),
            y1 = min(sero_lo), y2 = max(sero_hi),
            .by = metric) |>
  mutate(span = x2 - x,
         lo = pmax(0, pmin(y1, x2 - diag_expand * span)),
         hi = pmin(1, pmax(y2, x + diag_expand * span))) |>
  select(metric, x, lo, hi) |>
  pivot_longer(c(lo, hi), values_to = "sero")

p_sero <- ggplot(scat, aes(x, sero, colour = region)) +
  (if (diag_expand > 0) geom_blank(data = diag_lim, inherit.aes = FALSE,
                                   aes(x = x, y = sero))) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = x_lo, xend = x_hi, y = sero, yend = sero)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = x, xend = x, y = sero_lo, yend = sero_hi)) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, nrow = 1, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_region) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
  guides(colour = "none") +          # Region legend collected from panel A
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Seroprevalence") +
  theme_epi

Sero vs cum inc

sero_age_lo <- 9 / 12      # years; matches the EVC denominator
sero_age_hi <- 5
snap_week   <- max(weeks)  # last study week; coverage and EVC snapshot
n_min_round <- 5           # minimum sera per region within the last round
common_only <- TRUE

bin_all  <- as.Date(c("2024-07-01", "2024-10-01", "2025-01-01",
                      "2025-04-01", "2025-07-01", "2025-10-01"))
# The last four quarters give the same picture (check below), so only the
# final one is plotted
bin_keep <- as.Date(c("2024-07-01", "2024-10-01", "2025-10-01"))

inc_src <- snapshot_dist |>
  filter(bin %in% bin_all) |>
  mutate(region = as.character(assign_region(district)))

# CHECK: districts with no region drop out of every panel. Should be empty.
inc_src |> filter(is.na(region)) |> distinct(district)

# A tibble: 0 × 1
# ℹ 1 variable: district <chr>

# cum_n counts cases to the end of each quarter, so quarters are labelled by
# bin_end, as in panel A of the outbreak figure
inc_all <- inc_src |>
  summarise(cum_n = sum(cum_n), n_census = sum(n_census),
            .by = c(region, bin, bin_end)) |>
  mutate(
    inc    = cum_n / n_census * 1e5,
    inc_lo = qchisq(0.025, 2 * cum_n) / 2 / n_census * 1e5,
    inc_hi = qchisq(0.975, 2 * (cum_n + 1)) / 2 / n_census * 1e5
  )

# CHECK: with one x scale per quarter, a panel looks the same as the next when
# the regions keep their rank and relative position (pos). Same ranks and
# similar pos across the last four quarters = safe to merge them.
inc_all |>
  mutate(rank = rank(-inc),
         pos  = round((inc - min(inc)) / diff(range(inc)), 2),
         .by = bin_end) |>
  select(region, bin_end, rank, pos) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = bin_end, values_from = c(rank, pos))

# n = 5 per period, and the periods are nested cumulative counts, so these
# are not independent tests. cor.test() gives the exact p when there are no
# ties; the normal approximation (exact = FALSE) is poor at n = 5.
cor_inc <- dat_inc |>
  summarise(
    n   = sum(is.finite(x) & is.finite(inc)),
    rho = if (n >= 3) cor(x, inc, method = "spearman",
                          use = "complete.obs") else NA_real_,
    p   = if (n >= 3) suppressWarnings(
            cor.test(x, inc, method = "spearman")$p.value

# Fractional logit (quasibinomial GLM, logit link): the fitted curve stays
# inside 0-1 and bends near the bounds. Two parameters, like a straight line.
# Unlike Theil-Sen it is not robust to one outlying region.
fit_frac <- function(inc, x) {
  ok <- is.finite(inc) & is.finite(x)
  if (sum(ok) < 3) return(NULL)
  b    <- unname(coef(glm(x[ok] ~ inc[ok], family = quasibinomial)))
  grid <- seq(min(inc[ok]), max(inc[ok]), length.out = 100)
  tibble(inc = grid, x = plogis(b[1] + b[2] * grid))
}

fit_curve <- dat_inc |> reframe(fit_frac(inc, x), .by = c(metric, period))

# The logit link bends the curve, but only visibly when the fitted values span
# a wide part of 0-1. Per panel, in percentage points: how far the fitted
# value moves across the panel, the largest gap between the curve and the
# straight line joining its ends, and the largest gap to a linear fit.
curve_check <- function(inc, x) {
  ok <- is.finite(inc) & is.finite(x)
  if (sum(ok) < 3) return(NULL)
  b     <- coef(glm(x[ok] ~ inc[ok], family = quasibinomial))
  l     <- coef(lm(x[ok] ~ inc[ok]))
  grid  <- seq(min(inc[ok]), max(inc[ok]), length.out = 100)
  fit   <- plogis(b[1] + b[2] * grid)
  chord <- approx(range(grid), fit[c(1, 100)], grid)$y
  tibble(fit_range_pp = 100 * diff(range(fit)),
         bend_pp      = 100 * max(abs(fit - chord)),
         vs_linear_pp = 100 * max(abs(fit - (l[1] + l[2] * grid))))
}

dat_inc |> reframe(curve_check(inc, x), .by = c(metric, period))

text:
Under5: Sero vs cum

# ===========================================================================
# 14. UNDER-5 CUMULATIVE INCIDENCE BY REGION
# ===========================================================================
# The all-age version compares child immunity against an outbreak measured in
# the whole population. Restricting both numerator and denominator to young
# children makes the incidence measure match what the immunity measures
# describe.
 
case_age_lo <- 0     # years, inclusive
case_age_hi <- 5     # years, exclusive
 
# Setting case_age_lo <- 1 excludes infants, who are not yet MCV1-eligible and
# so sit outside the coverage and EVC denominators (9-59 months). That is the
# cleaner age match; 0-5 keeps the group epidemiologically complete.
 
dedupe_cases <- TRUE
 
# ---- duplicate records ----------------------------------------------------
 
df_ep2 |> summarise(rows = n(), unique_ids = n_distinct(id))
df_ep2 |> count(id) |> filter(n > 1) |> nrow()
 
# ---- census denominator ---------------------------------------------------
# Census age band k covers [k-1, k), so under 5 is bands 1:5, not 1:4.
 
census_u5 <- df_census |>
  filter(age >= case_age_lo + 1, age <= case_age_hi) |>
  summarise(n = sum(n), .by = district) |>
  mutate(district = merge_thuduc(clean_district(district)),
         region   = assign_region(district)) |>
  summarise(n_census = sum(n), .by = region) |>
  drop_na(region)
 
census_u5
 
# sanity: under-5s should be a few percent of the all-age total
tibble(u5 = sum(census_u5$n_census), all_age = sum(df_census$n)) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * u5 / all_age)
 
# ---- case numerator -------------------------------------------------------
 
cases_u5 <- df_ep2 |>
  (\(d) if (dedupe_cases) distinct(d, id, .keep_all = TRUE) else d)() |>
  filter(age >= case_age_lo, age < case_age_hi) |>
  mutate(district = merge_thuduc(.data[[col_district]]),
         region   = assign_region(district),
         date     = .data[[col_date]]) |>
  drop_na(region, date)
 
cases_u5 |> count(region)
cat("under-5 cases:", nrow(cases_u5), "of", nrow(df_ep2), "rows\n")
 
# ---- quarterly cumulative incidence ---------------------------------------
# Bins built from the full date range so the under-5 and all-age versions
# share a bin grid; regions with no cases in a quarter still get a row.
 
date_rng <- range(df_ep2[[col_date]], na.rm = TRUE)
bin_grid <- seq(floor_date(date_rng[1], "quarter"),
                floor_date(date_rng[2], "quarter"), by = "quarter")
 
inc_u5 <- cases_u5 |>
  mutate(bin = floor_date(date, "quarter")) |>
  count(region, bin) |>
  complete(region = census_u5$region, bin = bin_grid, fill = list(n = 0)) |>
  arrange(region, bin) |>
  mutate(cum_n = cumsum(n), .by = region) |>
  left_join(census_u5, by = "region") |>
  mutate(
    group  = as.character(region),
    inc    = cum_n / n_census * 1e5,
    inc_lo = qchisq(0.025, 2 * cum_n) / 2 / n_census * 1e5,
    inc_hi = qchisq(0.975, 2 * (cum_n + 1)) / 2 / n_census * 1e5
  )
 
inc_u5 |> select(group, bin, cum_n, n_census, inc) |> arrange(bin) |> print(n = Inf)
 
# ===========================================================================
# 15. IMMUNITY MEASURES VS UNDER-5 INCIDENCE
# ===========================================================================
# Reuses x_all from section 13 (coverage and EVC at snap_week, seroprevalence
# from each hospital's last collection period).
 
bin_keep <- as.Date(c("2024-07-01", "2024-10-01", "2025-01-01",
                      "2025-04-01", "2025-07-01", "2025-10-01"))
bin_lab  <- setNames(format(bin_keep, "%b %Y"), as.character(bin_keep))
 
dat_u5 <- x_all |>
  inner_join(inc_u5 |> filter(bin %in% bin_keep) |>
               select(group, bin, region, inc, inc_lo, inc_hi),
             by = "group") |>
  mutate(metric = factor(metric, levels = metric_lev),
         region = factor(as.character(region), levels = rank_order),
         bin    = factor(bin_lab[as.character(bin)], levels = unname(bin_lab)))
 
dat_u5 |> summarise(n = n(), .by = c(metric, bin)) |> print(n = Inf)
 
# ---- Spearman rho ---------------------------------------------------------
# Five regions per panel, and the six bins are nested cumulative counts, so
# read each row as a trajectory rather than as six independent tests.
 
cor_u5 <- dat_u5 |>
  summarise(
    n   = sum(is.finite(x) & is.finite(inc)),
    rho = if (n[1] >= 3) cor(x, inc, method = "spearman",
                             use = "complete.obs") else NA_real_,
    p   = if (n[1] >= 3) suppressWarnings(
            cor.test(x, inc, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)$p.value
          ) else NA_real_,
    .by = c(metric, bin)
  ) |>
  mutate(lab = if_else(is.na(rho), "rho = NA",
                       sprintf("rho = %.2f\np = %.3f", rho, p)))
 
cor_u5 |> print(n = Inf)
 
# side by side with the all-age version, if section 13 was run
if (exists("cor_inc_all")) {
  cor_inc_all |>
    select(metric, bin, rho_all = rho) |>
    left_join(cor_u5 |> select(metric, bin, rho_u5 = rho), by = c("metric", "bin")) |>
    print(n = Inf)
}
 
# ---- Theil-Sen line, consistent with a rank correlation -------------------
 
theil_sen <- function(x, y) {
  ok <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(y)
  x <- x[ok]; y <- y[ok]
  if (length(x) < 3) return(NULL)
  cb   <- combn(length(x), 2)
  dx   <- x[cb[2, ]] - x[cb[1, ]]
  dy   <- y[cb[2, ]] - y[cb[1, ]]
  keep <- dx != 0
  if (!any(keep)) return(NULL)
  b <- median(dy[keep] / dx[keep])
  tibble(a = median(y - b * x), b = b, x1 = min(x), x2 = max(x))
}
 
fit_u5 <- dat_u5 |>
  reframe(theil_sen(inc, x), .by = c(metric, bin)) |>
  transmute(metric, bin, inc = x1, inc_end = x2,
            x = a + b * x1, x_end = a + b * x2)
 
# ---- figure ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Horizontal bars: exact 95% Poisson CI for the incidence rate.
# Vertical bars: 95% VE-parameter interval (EVC) or exact 95% CI
# (seroprevalence). Coverage is a registry census and carries no bar.
# Dashed line: Theil-Sen fit, an aid to reading direction, not a model.
 
p_u5 <- ggplot(dat_u5, aes(inc, x, colour = region)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = inc_lo, xend = inc_hi, y = x, yend = x)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = inc, xend = inc, y = x_lo, yend = x_hi), na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_segment(data = fit_u5, inherit.aes = FALSE,
               aes(x = inc, xend = inc_end, y = x, yend = x_end),
               linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  geom_text(data = cor_u5, aes(x = -Inf, y = Inf, label = lab),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "black", hjust = -0.08, vjust = 1.2,
            lineheight = 0.9) +
  facet_grid(metric ~ bin, scales = "free", switch = "y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_region) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Cumulative incidence per 100,000 children under 5",
       y = NULL, colour = "Region") +
  theme_epi() +
  theme(strip.placement = "inside")
 
p_u5
 
ggsave("figs/chap1/fig_immunity_vs_incidence_u5.png", p_u5,
       width = 9.5, height = 6.5, dpi = 300)

df_top <- df_case |>
  as_tibble() |>
  filter(!is.na(source_province), !is.na(onset_date), !is.na(province)) |>
  mutate(onset_date = as.Date(onset_date), province = as.character(province)) |>
  filter(onset_date >= x_lims[1], onset_date <= x_lims[2])

provs <- df_top |> count(province, sort = TRUE) |> slice_head(n = n_provs) |> pull(province)

df_top <- df_top |>
  filter(province %in% provs) |>
  filter(n() >= min_n, .by = c(province, source_province)) |>
  filter(any(source_province == "community"), .by = province)

# ---- one grid, one bandwidth, one kernel matrix per province x source --------
kde_grid <- seq(as.numeric(x_lims[1]), as.numeric(x_lims[2]), length.out = grid_n)

dens_tbl <- df_top |>
  summarise(n = n(), x = list(as.numeric(onset_date)), .by = c(province, source_province)) |>
  mutate(K      = map(x, \(v) dnorm(outer(v, kde_grid, "-"), sd = bw_days)),  # n x grid
         dens_v = map(K, colMeans),
         dens_v = if (weight_by_n) map2(dens_v, n, \(v, k) v * k) else dens_v)

gmax <- max(unlist(dens_tbl$dens_v))                  # single global constant

# ---- peaks and bootstrap ----------------------------------------------------
boot_modes <- function(K, nrep) {
  n <- nrow(K)
  W <- t(rmultinom(nrep, n, rep.int(1 / n, n)))       # nrep x n resample counts
  kde_grid[max.col(W %*% K, ties.method = "first")]
}

pk <- dens_tbl |>
  mutate(i      = map_int(dens_v, which.max),
         peak_x = kde_grid[i],
         peak_h = map2_dbl(dens_v, i, \(v, j) v[j]) / gmax * ridge_scale,
         boot   = map(K, boot_modes, nrep = n_boot))

# how stable is each peak? ratio2 near 1 means two rival modes of similar height
diag_tbl <- dens_tbl |>
  mutate(lm_idx  = map(dens_v, \(v) which(diff(sign(diff(v))) == -2) + 1),
         n_modes = map_int(lm_idx, length),
         ratio2  = map2_dbl(dens_v, lm_idx,
                            \(v, j) if (length(j) < 2) 0 else
                              {h <- sort(v[j], decreasing = TRUE); h[2] / h[1]})) |>
  select(province, source_province, n, n_modes, ratio2) |>
  arrange(desc(ratio2))

# ---- helpers ----------------------------------------------------------------
yn <- function(x) {
  if (is.logical(x)) return(x)
  if (is.numeric(x)) return(x == 1)
  s <- tolower(trimws(as.character(x)))
  out <- rep(NA, length(s))
  out[s %in% c("yes", "y", "1", "true", "t")]  <- TRUE
  out[s %in% c("no",  "n", "0", "false", "f")] <- FALSE
  out
}

tidy_or <- function(m, keep = NULL) {
  ct  <- summary(m)$coefficients
  est <- ct[, 1]; se <- ct[, 2]
  sel <- !grepl("ns\\(|Intercept", rownames(ct))
  out <- tibble(term = rownames(ct)[sel],
                or = exp(est[sel]),
                lo = exp(est[sel] - 1.96 * se[sel]),
                hi = exp(est[sel] + 1.96 * se[sel]),
                p  = 2 * pnorm(-abs(est[sel] / se[sel])),
                n  = stats::nobs(m)) |>
    mutate(txt = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", or, lo, hi))
  if (is.null(keep)) out else filter(out, term %in% keep)
}

lrt_p <- function(full, red) anova(red, full, test = "LRT")[2, "Pr(>Chi)"]

desc_out <- function(dat, v, outcome) {
  lv <- levels(dat[[v]])
  d <- dat |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[v]])) |>
    summarise(n_tot = n(), n_pos = sum(.data[[outcome]]), .by = all_of(v)) |>
    rename(level = 1) |>
    mutate(level = as.character(level))
  if (!is.null(lv)) d <- d |> arrange(match(level, lv))
  d |> mutate(term = paste0(v, level),
              cell = sprintf("%d/%d (%.1f%%)", n_pos, n_tot, 100 * n_pos / n_tot))
}

# one header row, then one indented row per level, ORs taken from `adj`
blk <- function(dat, v, header, outcome, adj) {
  desc_out(dat, v, outcome) |>
    left_join(adj |> select(term, a = txt), by = "term") |>
    mutate(a = replace_na(a, "1 (ref)")) |>
    transmute(Characteristic = paste0("  ", level), n_out = cell, Adjusted = a) |>
    (\(d) bind_rows(tibble(Characteristic = header, n_out = "", Adjusted = ""), d))()
}

## derived quantities (thesis Section 4.3.5); s_C0, s_H0 and xi_alpha are fixed.
## One function, so the posterior draws and the MAP use the same formulas.
add_derived <- function(d) {
  d |>
    mutate(
      beta_H  = kappa * beta_C,
      D_C     = (eta + delta) / (eta + xi_alpha + delta) * (1 / eta + (1 - p_a) / gamma),
      R0C     = beta_C * D_C,             # community, everyone susceptible
      R_C_eff = s_C0 * R0C,               # community, at the start of the outbreak
      R0H     = beta_H * ((eta + xi_alpha) / (eta * (eta + xi_alpha + delta)) +
                  (1 - p_i_fixed) / gamma * (eta + xi_alpha + p_a * delta) /
                  (eta + xi_alpha + delta)),
      per_case_ratio = kappa * s_H0 / s_C0   # infections per case, H relative to C
    )
}

post <- getSample(fit) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  setNames(par_names) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  add_derived()

## MAP: the posterior draw with the highest log posterior (BayesianTools::MAP).
## Derived quantities are computed at this one parameter set.
best    <- MAP(fit)
map_row <- as_tibble_row(best$parametersMAP[par_names]) |> add_derived()

vars <- c("beta_C", "beta_H", "R0C", "R_C_eff", "R0H", "kappa", "p_a",
          "per_case_ratio", "seed",
          intersect(c("rho", "phi", "phi_in", "phi_out"), names(post)))

map_long <- map_row |>
  select(all_of(vars)) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "par", values_to = "MAP")

  group_by(par = factor(par, levels = vars)) |>

  relocate(MAP, .after = par) |>
  mutate(crI = paste0(sprintf("%.2f", lo), "-", sprintf("%.2f", hi))) |>

set.seed(20260921)
wk2date <- function(w) t0_date + 7 * w

## posterior predictive draws. y_rep is the weekly total; in the split option it
## is the sum of the inpatient and outpatient draws.
pp <- post |>
  slice_sample(n = 1000) |>
  mutate(draw = row_number()) |>
  group_split(draw) |>
  map_dfr(function(d) {
    par <- unlist(d[par_names])
    s <- run_model(par, n_weeks, full = TRUE)
    if (is.null(s)) return(NULL)
    rho <- if (fit_rho) d$rho else 1

    res <- tibble(draw   = d$draw,
                  week   = s$week,
                  mu_in  = rho * s$adm,
                  mu_out = rho * s$out,
                  mu     = mu_in + mu_out,
                  share  = s$adm / (s$adm + s$out),
                  noso   = s$noso)

    if (obs_model == "total") {
      res |> mutate(y_rep = rnbinom(n(), mu = mu, size = d$phi))
    } else {
      res |> mutate(y_in  = rnbinom(n(), mu = mu_in,  size = d$phi_in),
                    y_out = rnbinom(n(), mu = mu_out, size = d$phi_out),
                    y_rep = y_in + y_out)
    }
  })

band <- pp |>
  group_by(week) |>
  summarise(lo95 = hdi(y_rep)[["lo"]],      hi95 = hdi(y_rep)[["hi"]],
            lo50 = hdi(y_rep, 0.5)[["lo"]], hi50 = hdi(y_rep, 0.5)[["hi"]],
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(date = wk2date(week))

## the MAP: expected weekly cases (the line in A), the negative binomial SD at
## that mean, and the 95% HDI of 10,000 negative binomial draws (B)
p_map   <- best$parametersMAP
s_map   <- run_model(p_map, n_weeks, full = TRUE)
rho_map <- if (fit_rho) p_map[["rho"]] else 1

nb_draws <- function(mu_in, mu_out, n = 1e4) {
  if (obs_model == "total") {
    rnbinom(n, mu = mu_in + mu_out, size = p_map[["phi"]])
  } else {
    rnbinom(n, mu = mu_in,  size = p_map[["phi_in"]]) +
      rnbinom(n, mu = mu_out, size = p_map[["phi_out"]])
  }
}

map_week <- tibble(week   = s_map$week,
                   mu_in  = rho_map * s_map$adm,
                   mu_out = rho_map * s_map$out) |>
  mutate(mu  = mu_in + mu_out,
         sd  = if (obs_model == "total") sqrt(mu + mu^2 / p_map[["phi"]]) else
                 sqrt(mu_in + mu_in^2 / p_map[["phi_in"]] + mu_out + mu_out^2 / p_map[["phi_out"]]),
         int = map2(mu_in, mu_out, \(a, b) hdi(nb_draws(a, b))),
         date = wk2date(week)) |>
  unnest_wider(int)

  date_axis +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +   # room for the label
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Weekly cases") +
  theme_thesis


# =============================================================================
# Residuals
#
# Pearson residuals at the MAP: observed minus the expected weekly cases at the
# MAP, divided by the negative binomial SD at the MAP. The dotted lines are the
# 95% HDI of the negative binomial at the MAP, on the same scale. Runs of
# same-signed residuals mean structure the model does not capture.
# =============================================================================

resid_df <- obs_d |>
  left_join(map_week |> select(week, mu, sd, lo, hi), by = c("t_week" = "week")) |>
  mutate(resid = (total - mu) / sd,   # Pearson residual at the MAP
         lo    = (lo - mu) / sd,      # 95% HDI of the negative binomial at the MAP
         hi    = (hi - mu) / sd)

fig_resid <- ggplot(resid_df, aes(date, resid)) +
  campaign_layer +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_line(aes(y = lo), linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_line(aes(y = hi), linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, fill = "white", size = 1.3, stroke = 0.5) +
  date_axis +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Residual") +
  theme_thesis


# =============================================================================
# Posterior distributions and correlations
#
# Diagonal: posterior and prior densities, both scaled by the posterior's peak,
# so a prior that the data overrode reads as flat. Lower triangle: 2,000 joint
# draws, minus the few outside the axis range. Upper triangle: posterior
# correlation.
# =============================================================================

post_p  <- post |> select(all_of(par_names))
prior_p <- prior_sampler(20000) |> as.data.frame() |> setNames(par_names)

## axis range per parameter: the central 99% of the posterior
lo  <- map_dbl(post_p, ~ quantile(.x, 0.005))
hi  <- map_dbl(post_p, ~ quantile(.x, 0.995))
mid <- (lo + hi) / 2

cells <- expand_grid(xvar = par_names, yvar = par_names) |>
  mutate(i = match(yvar, par_names), j = match(xvar, par_names))

as_panel <- function(d) {
  d |> mutate(xvar = factor(xvar, levels = par_names),
              yvar = factor(yvar, levels = par_names))
}

thin <- post_p |> slice_sample(n = 2000)

## a draw outside the range would stretch its row or column, so drop it
pts <- cells |>
  filter(i > j) |>
  mutate(xy = map2(xvar, yvar, ~ tibble(x = thin[[.x]], y = thin[[.y]]))) |>
  unnest(xy) |>
  filter(x >= lo[xvar], x <= hi[xvar], y >= lo[yvar], y <= hi[yvar]) |>
  as_panel()

dens <- map_dfr(par_names, function(p) {
  d_post <- density(post_p[[p]],  from = lo[[p]], to = hi[[p]], n = 200)
  d_pri  <- density(prior_p[[p]], from = lo[[p]], to = hi[[p]], n = 200)
  k <- 0.95 * (hi[[p]] - lo[[p]]) / max(d_post$y)
  bind_rows(tibble(dist = "Posterior", x = d_post$x, y = lo[[p]] + k * d_post$y),
            tibble(dist = "Prior",     x = d_pri$x,  y = lo[[p]] + k * d_pri$y)) |>
    mutate(xvar = p, yvar = p)
}) |>
  as_panel()

cors <- cells |>
  filter(i < j) |>
  mutate(r = map2_dbl(xvar, yvar, ~ cor(post_p[[.x]], post_p[[.y]])),
         x = mid[xvar], y = mid[yvar]) |>
  as_panel()

## at most two ticks per axis, away from the panel edges. If the two ticks are
## closer than 45% of the range, their labels can touch, so keep only the tick
## nearer the middle.
two_breaks <- function(l) {
  b <- pretty(l, n = 4)
  b <- b[b > l[1] + 0.1 * diff(l) & b < l[2] - 0.1 * diff(l)]
  if (length(b) > 2) b <- b[c(1, length(b))]
  if (length(b) == 2 && diff(b) < 0.45 * diff(l)) b <- b[which.min(abs(b - mean(l)))]
  b
}

## hold every row and column to its parameter's range
limits <- bind_rows(
  cells |> transmute(xvar, yvar, x = lo[xvar], y = lo[yvar]),
  cells |> transmute(xvar, yvar, x = hi[xvar], y = hi[yvar])
) |>
  as_panel()

fig_corner <- ggplot() +
  geom_blank(data = limits, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_rect(data = cors, aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
                             fill = r)) +
  geom_text(data = cors, aes(x, y, label = sprintf("%.2f", r),
                             colour = abs(r) > 0.6), size = 2.6) +
  geom_point(data = pts, aes(x, y), size = 0.2, alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(data = dens, aes(x, y, linetype = dist), linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_grid(yvar ~ xvar, scales = "free", switch = "both",
             labeller = as_labeller(lbl, default = label_parsed)) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B",
                       limits = c(-1, 1), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "black", `TRUE` = "white"),
                      guide = "none") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(Posterior = "solid", Prior = "dashed"),
                        name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = two_breaks,
                     guide = guide_axis(check.overlap = TRUE)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = two_breaks,
                     guide = guide_axis(check.overlap = TRUE)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_thesis +
  theme(aspect.ratio      = 1,                        # square cells
        strip.placement   = "outside",
        strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0),  # horizontal row labels
        panel.border      = element_rect(colour = "grey75", fill = NA),
        axis.line         = element_blank(),
        axis.text         = element_text(size = 6),
        panel.spacing     = unit(1.2, "mm"),
        legend.position   = "right")                  # the empty space on the right

by_run <- map_dfr(seq_along(fit), function(i) {

title: Result 3: Hospital-community model
text:
Force of infection

set.seed(20260922)
n_draws <- 1000       # 200 is enough while adjusting the layout

## own names for the theme and the date axis of these figures, so theme_thesis
## and date_axis of the calibration figure stay as Part 1 set them
theme_plain <- theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
        legend.title     = element_blank())

narrow <- theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 8))   # three panels in a row

date_axis_6m <- list(
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "6 months", date_labels = "%b\n%Y"),
  coord_cartesian(xlim = range(obs$week))
)

setting_col <- c(Hospital = "#BC3C29", Community = "#0072B5")
kappa_col   <- "#E18727"
prev_col    <- "#7876B1"   # infectious prevalence ratio, in panels A and D

x_right <- max(obs$week)   # labels end here, inside the visible range

## ---- simulate each posterior draw -------------------------------------------
par_of <- function(d) {
  c(setNames(as.numeric(d[par_names]), par_names), p_i = p_i_fixed)
}

## model day t is the date t0_date + 7 + t: wk2date() labels model week w with
## t0_date + 7 * w, the Monday that starts it, and week 1 starts on day 0
trajectory <- function(par, days = n_weeks * 7) {
  sol <- solve_model(par, 0:days)
  if (is.null(sol)) return(NULL)
  beta_C <- par[["beta_C"]]
  beta_H <- par[["kappa"]] * beta_C
  as.data.frame(sol) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    transmute(
      date     = t0_date + 7 + time,
      prev_C   = (I_C_pre + I_C_post) / (S_C + E_C + I_C_pre + I_C_post + R_C),
      prev_H   = (I_H_pre + I_H_post) / (S_H + E_H + I_H_pre + I_H_post + R_H),
      s_C      = S_C / (S_C + E_C + I_C_pre + I_C_post + R_C),
      s_H      = S_H / (S_H + E_H + I_H_pre + I_H_post + R_H),
      lambda_C = beta_C * prev_C,
      lambda_H = beta_H * prev_H
    )
}

traj <- post |>
  slice_sample(n = n_draws) |>
  mutate(draw = row_number()) |>
  group_split(draw) |>
  map_dfr(function(d) {
    s <- trajectory(par_of(d))
    if (is.null(s)) return(NULL)
    s |> mutate(draw = d$draw, kappa = d$kappa, beta_C = d$beta_C)
  })

## dates on which the outbreak is under way (median community prevalence above
## 1 in 100,000); ratios of near-zero prevalences are not meaningful
window <- traj |>
  group_by(date) |>
  summarise(p = median(prev_C), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(p > 1e-5) |>
  pull(date)

## each draw at its own peak of community prevalence, for the 95% HDI of kappa
## in A and of every ratio in D
peaks <- traj |>
  group_by(draw) |>
  slice_max(prev_C, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()

## the MAP parameter set (Posterior section): its trajectory gives every line
## and point in the figure; the draws give the 95% HDI around them
traj_map <- trajectory(par_of(map_row)) |>
  mutate(kappa = map_row$kappa)

peak_map  <- traj_map |> slice_max(prev_C, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
peak_date <- peak_map$date

## ---- A: the result ------------------------------------------------------------
## the force of infection ratio is the product of the two other ratios in the
## panel: lambda_H / lambda_C = kappa x P, with P the infectious prevalence ratio
ratio_t <- traj |>                                  # 95% HDI, day by day
  filter(date %in% window) |>
  mutate(foi  = lambda_H / lambda_C,
         prev = prev_H / prev_C) |>
  pivot_longer(c(foi, prev), names_to = "ratio") |>
  group_by(ratio, date) |>
  summarise(lo = hdi_log(value)[["lo"]],
            hi = hdi_log(value)[["hi"]], .groups = "drop")

ratio_map <- traj_map |>                            # the MAP lines
  filter(date %in% window) |>
  transmute(date,
            foi  = lambda_H / lambda_C,
            prev = prev_H / prev_C) |>
  pivot_longer(-date, names_to = "ratio", values_to = "map")

## kappa: the MAP value, with the 95% HDI of the draws
kq <- c(hdi_log(peaks$kappa)[["lo"]], map_row$kappa, hdi_log(peaks$kappa)[["hi"]])

## where each line ends, to place its label
end_y <- ratio_map |>
  filter(date <= x_right) |>
  group_by(ratio) |>
  slice_max(date, n = 1) |>
  select(ratio, map) |>
  deframe()

## Each label goes on the side of its line with more room. On the log scale, the
## room above the kappa x P line (up to P) and above the kappa line (up to 1) is a
## factor of 1 / kappa. The room below is a factor of kappa x P (down to 1) and of
## kappa / the lower end of its HDI (down to the bottom of its band).
vj <- function(above) if (above) -0.3 else 1.3
vj_foi   <- vj(1 / kq[[2]] > end_y[["foi"]])
vj_kappa <- vj(1 / kq[[2]] > kq[[2]] / kq[[1]])

pA <- ggplot(mapping = aes(date)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = peak_date, linetype = "dotted") +
  annotate("rect", xmin = min(window), xmax = max(window),
           ymin = kq[[1]], ymax = kq[[3]], fill = kappa_col, alpha = 0.25) +
  annotate("segment", x = min(window), xend = max(window),
           y = kq[[2]], yend = kq[[2]], colour = kappa_col, linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_ribbon(data = ratio_t, aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi, fill = ratio), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(data = ratio_map, aes(y = map, colour = ratio), linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(foi = "grey40", prev = prev_col), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(foi = "black", prev = prev_col), guide = "none") +
  annotate("text", x = x_right, y = end_y[["prev"]], label = "Prevalence",
           colour = prev_col, hjust = 1, vjust = -0.3, size = 2.8) +
  annotate("text", x = x_right, y = end_y[["foi"]], label = "FOI",
           hjust = 1, vjust = vj_foi, size = 2.8) +
  annotate("text", x = x_right, y = kq[[2]], label = "Ratio \u03ba",
           colour = kappa_col, hjust = 1, vjust = vj_kappa, size = 2.8) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE),
                expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.15))) +   # room for the top label
  date_axis_6m +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Hospital / community") +
  theme_plain +
  narrow

## ---- B and C: the two settings side by side ---------------------------------
## B is prevalence (a component), C the force of infection (the product), in the
## same order as panel D
long <- traj |>
  filter(date %in% window) |>
  transmute(draw, date,
            foi_Community  = 1000 * lambda_C, foi_Hospital  = 1000 * lambda_H,
            prev_Community = 1000 * prev_C,   prev_Hospital = 1000 * prev_H) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(draw, date), names_to = c("quantity", "setting"),
               names_sep = "_") |>
  group_by(quantity, setting, date) |>
  summarise(lo = hdi_log(value)[["lo"]],
            hi = hdi_log(value)[["hi"]], .groups = "drop")

long_map <- traj_map |>
  filter(date %in% window) |>
  transmute(date,
            foi_Community  = 1000 * lambda_C, foi_Hospital  = 1000 * lambda_H,
            prev_Community = 1000 * prev_C,   prev_Hospital = 1000 * prev_H) |>
  pivot_longer(-date, names_to = c("quantity", "setting"), names_sep = "_",
               values_to = "map")

## one shared legend for B and C (collected in the assembly below)
time_panel <- function(q, ylab) {
  ggplot(mapping = aes(date, colour = setting, fill = setting)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = peak_date, linetype = "dotted") +
    geom_ribbon(data = filter(long, quantity == q),
                aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25, colour = NA) +
    geom_line(data = filter(long_map, quantity == q),
              aes(y = map), linewidth = 0.6) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = setting_col) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = setting_col) +
    scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
    date_axis_6m +
    labs(x = NULL, y = ylab) +
    theme_plain +
    narrow
}

pB <- time_panel("prev", "Prevalence\nper 1,000")
pC <- time_panel("foi",  "Force of infection\n(per 1,000 per day)")

## ---- D: how the pieces combine, at the peak ---------------------------------
## each component gets a letter, and each product shows which letters multiply.
## The products follow the argument: kappa x P is the risk to a susceptible
## child; multiplying by s gives the risk to any child in the setting.
labels_D <- c(
  kappa = "Infectious contact rate ratio, \u03ba",
  prev  = "Infectious prevalence, P",
  sus   = "Susceptible proportion, s",
  foi   = "Force of infection, \u03ba \u00d7 P",
  inc   = "Incidence, \u03ba \u00d7 P \u00d7 s"
)

ratios_D <- function(d) {
  d |>
    transmute(kappa,
              prev = prev_H / prev_C,
              sus  = s_H / s_C,
              foi  = kappa * prev,
              inc  = kappa * prev * sus) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "factor")
}

decomp <- ratios_D(peaks) |>                        # 95% HDI, each draw at its peak
  group_by(factor) |>
  summarise(lo    = hdi_log(value)[["lo"]],
            hi    = hdi_log(value)[["hi"]],
            p_gt1 = mean(value > 1), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(ratios_D(peak_map) |> rename(map = value),   # the MAP, at its peak
            by = "factor") |>
  mutate(type   = if_else(factor %in% c("kappa", "prev", "sus"),
                          "Components", "Products"),
         colour = case_when(factor == "kappa" ~ kappa_col,
                            factor == "prev"  ~ prev_col,
                            TRUE              ~ "black"),
         label  = factor(labels_D[factor], levels = rev(labels_D)))

pD <- ggplot(decomp, aes(map, label, colour = colour)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi, shape = type), fill = "white") +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(Components = 16, Products = 23), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  facet_grid(type ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Ratio hospital / community at the peak", y = NULL) +
  theme_plain +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0))

## ---- assemble -----------------------------------------------------------------

text:
Sensitivity analysis

R0H parameters

## ---- R_0H and its partial derivatives ------------------------------------------
r0h <- function(beta_H, eta, gamma, delta, xi_alpha, p_a, p_i) {
  beta_H * ((eta + xi_alpha) / (eta * (eta + xi_alpha + delta)) +
              (1 - p_i) / gamma * (eta + xi_alpha + p_a * delta) / (eta + xi_alpha + delta))
}

r0h_slope <- function(par, beta_H, eta, gamma, delta, xi_alpha, p_a, p_i) {
  switch(par,
    beta_H = (eta + xi_alpha) / (eta * (eta + xi_alpha + delta)) +
               (1 - p_i) / gamma * (eta + xi_alpha + p_a * delta) / (eta + xi_alpha + delta),
    delta  = -beta_H * (eta + xi_alpha) / (eta + xi_alpha + delta)^2 *
               (1 / eta + (1 - p_i) * (1 - p_a) / gamma),
    p_a    = beta_H * (1 - p_i) * delta / (gamma * (eta + xi_alpha + delta)),
    p_i    = -beta_H * (eta + xi_alpha + p_a * delta) / (gamma * (eta + xi_alpha + delta))
  )
}

## ---- baseline values -----------------------------------------------------------
## beta_C, kappa and p_a: the MAP column of the posterior summary
base <- list(
  beta_H   = 0.612 * 2.573,   # kappa * beta_C
  eta      = 1 / 4,           # pre-rash -> post-rash
  gamma    = 1 / 4,           # post-rash -> removed
  delta    = 1 / 5.2,         # TO CONFIRM: mean length of stay 5.2 days
  xi_alpha = 0.001289992,     # fixed: setting alpha to 0 lowers R_0H by only 0.2%
  p_a      = 0.512,
  p_i      = 0.9              # assumption
)
R0H_base <- do.call(r0h, base)

## ---- range for each parameter (theoretical) ------------------------------------
## p_a, p_i: the full range of a probability, 0 to 1
## delta:    length of stay from 2 days to 30 days, so delta from 1/30 to 1/2
## beta_H:   no natural limits, so the 95% HDI of kappa, times the MAP of beta_C
##           (with posterior draws, use the 95% HDI of kappa * beta_C)
## label_low, label_high: the parameter value printed at each end of the bar
kappa_hdi <- c(0.12, 0.95)   # TO UPDATE: the 95% HDI of kappa (posterior table)
bH        <- c(0.34, 2.32) # times the MAP of beta_C
pars <- tribble(
  ~par,     ~name,                     ~sym,      ~low,   ~high,  ~label_low,             ~label_high,
  "beta_H", "Transmission rate",       "beta[H]", bH[1],  bH[2],  sprintf("%.2f", bH[1]), sprintf("%.2f", bH[2]),
  "delta",  "Discharge rate",          "delta",   1 / 30, 1 / 2,  "30-day stay",          "2-day stay",
  "p_a",    "Admission at rash onset", "p[a]",    0,      1,      "0",                    "1",
  "p_i",    "Isolation",               "p[i]",    0,      1,      "0",                    "1"
)

## ---- slope and range for each parameter ----------------------------------------
## R_0H changes in one direction across each range, so its lowest and highest
## values are at the two ends
pars <- pars |>
  mutate(base_value = map_dbl(par, \(p) base[[p]]),
         slope      = map_dbl(par, \(p) do.call(r0h_slope, c(list(par = p), base))),
         elasticity = slope * base_value / R0H_base,
         R0H_low    = map2_dbl(par, low,  \(p, v) do.call(r0h, replace(base, p, v))),
         R0H_high   = map2_dbl(par, high, \(p, v) do.call(r0h, replace(base, p, v))),
         R0H_min    = pmin(R0H_low, R0H_high),
         R0H_max    = pmax(R0H_low, R0H_high),
         label_min  = if_else(R0H_low < R0H_high, label_low, label_high),
         label_max  = if_else(R0H_low < R0H_high, label_high, label_low),
         change     = R0H_max - R0H_min,
         ## exact % change in R_0H for a 10% increase in the parameter
         pct_10     = map2_dbl(par, base_value * 1.1,
                               \(p, v) 100 * (do.call(r0h, replace(base, p, v)) / R0H_base - 1))) |>
  arrange(change) |>                                  # largest at the top of the plot
  mutate(row = fct_inorder(sym))                      # symbol only, e.g. beta[H]

## check: each elasticity against a numerical one, from R_0H at x * (1 +/- 1e-6)
elasticity_numeric <- function(p, h = 1e-6) {
  up   <- do.call(r0h, replace(base, p, base[[p]] * (1 + h)))
  down <- do.call(r0h, replace(base, p, base[[p]] * (1 - h)))
  (up - down) / (2 * h * R0H_base)
}
stopifnot(all(abs(map_dbl(pars$par, elasticity_numeric) - pars$elasticity) < 1e-6))

## numbers for the text and the table
pars |>
  select(par, base_value, slope, elasticity, pct_10, R0H_min, R0H_max, change) |>
  arrange(desc(change)) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)))

## panel B: R_0H across each parameter's range
p_range <- ggplot(pars, aes(y = row)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = R0H_min, xmax = R0H_max), orientation = "y",
                width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.8, colour = blue) +
  geom_point(aes(x = R0H_base), size = 2.6, colour = blue) +

## hospital susceptibility for a given community susceptibility and xi, and xi
## for a given s_C0 and s_H0 (the inverse)
s_H_from <- function(s_C0, xi) xi * s_C0 / (1 - s_C0 + xi * s_C0)
xi_from  <- function(s_C0, s_H0) s_H0 * (1 - s_C0) / (s_C0 * (1 - s_H0))

## admission rates of immune (alpha) and susceptible (xi * alpha) children:
##   alpha = alpha_bar / (1 + s_C0 * (xi - 1))
admission <- function(s_C0, xi) {
  alpha <- alpha_bar / (1 + s_C0 * (xi - 1))
  c(alpha = alpha, xi_alpha = xi * alpha)
}

## ---- one run -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
## fade-out: fewer than 0.1 latent or infectious children. Isolated children
## (Q) do not transmit, so they are not counted.
gone <- function(t, y, p) {
  sum(y[c("E_C", "I_C_pre", "I_C_post", "E_H", "I_H_pre", "I_H_post")]) - 0.1
}

## infections caused by one imported case (total), and the day of fade-out
## (t_fade: NA when the threshold is not reached within max_days, 50 years).
## counters = TRUE returns the final counters instead: infections acquired in
## the community (cum_inf_C) and in hospital (cum_noso), rash onsets and
## admissions with rash.
infections <- function(s_C0, xi, kappa, p_i, los, hospital = TRUE,
                       max_days = 365 * 50, counters = FALSE) {
  delta <- 1 / los
  N_H   <- alpha_bar * N / (delta + alpha_bar)   # inpatients that balance admissions and discharges
  s_H0  <- s_H_from(s_C0, xi)
  adm   <- admission(s_C0, xi)
  
  N_h <- if (hospital) N_H else 0
  N_c <- N - N_h
  s_c <- if (hospital) s_C0 else (s_C0 * (N - N_H) + s_H0 * N_H) / N   # inpatients join the community
  
  y0 <- c(S_C = s_c * N_c - 1, E_C = 1, I_C_pre = 0, I_C_post = 0,
          R_C = (1 - s_c) * N_c,
          S_H = s_H0 * N_h, E_H = 0, I_H_pre = 0, I_H_post = 0, Q = 0,
          R_H = (1 - s_H0) * N_h,
          cum_onset_C = 0, cum_onset_H = 0, cum_noso = 0, cum_adm_rash = 0,
          cum_inf_C = 0)[state_names]
  
  p <- c(beta_C   = beta_C,
         beta_H   = if (hospital) kappa * beta_C else 0,
         xi_alpha = if (hospital) adm[["xi_alpha"]] else 0,
         alpha    = if (hospital) adm[["alpha"]] else 0,
         p_a      = if (hospital) p_a else 0,
         delta    = if (hospital) delta else 0,
         p_i = p_i, delta_M = delta_M,
         sigma = sigma, eta = eta, gamma = gamma)
  
  out <- ode(y0, c(0, max_days), measles_ode, p, rootfunc = gone,
             atol = 1e-6, rtol = 1e-8)
  end <- out[nrow(out), ]
  if (counters) return(end[c("cum_inf_C", "cum_noso", "cum_onset_C", "cum_onset_H", "cum_adm_rash")])
  troot <- attr(out, "troot")   # the time of the root; NULL if none was found
  c(total  = end[["cum_inf_C"]] + end[["cum_noso"]],
    t_fade = if (length(troot) > 0) troot[[1]] else NA)
}

## the lowest isolation at which the hospital stops amplifying an imported case:
## it no longer adds infections (when there is an outbreak of 10 or more without
## the hospital) or no longer causes such an outbreak (when there is not).
## 0: no isolation needed; NA: amplifies even with p_i = 1.
iso_needed <- function(s_C0, s_H0, kappa) {
  xi_h   <- xi_from(s_C0, s_H0)
  none   <- infections(s_C0, xi_h, 0, 0, los_fix, hospital = FALSE)[["total"]]
  target <- if (none >= outbreak_size) none else outbreak_size
  f <- \(p) infections(s_C0, xi_h, kappa, p, los_fix)[["total"]] - target
  if (f(0) <= 0) return(0)
  if (f(1) > 0)  return(NA)
  uniroot(f, c(0, 1), tol = 0.001)$root
}
